articleTitle: An Efficiency Optimized Gear-Shift Map to Maximise the Performance of a Modular E-Axle
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper summarizes the development of an efficiency optimized gear-shift map to maximize the performance of a 9-tonne modular e-axle for all-terrain heavy-duty vehicles. Raw power loss data for an inverter and motor system is analyzed and processed, resulting in component power loss and efficiency maps for each component along with combined inverter and motor system. The e-axle efficiency maps for each gear were calculated and mapped to a common set of lookup vectors before the most efficient gear for each operating point was selected. The usefulness of the e-axle power loss maps for sizing vehicle cooling packs was demonstrated through a simulation of the California Air Research Board (CARB) Heavy Heavy-Duty Diesel Truck (HHDDT) Composite Cycle.

articleTitle: Implementing European Experiences of Energy Community Strategy Based on High Utilization of Renewable Energy Sources to Distributed Power Grids in Ukrainian Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper focuses on the project of photovoltaic systems for the power supply of the energy communities (EC) in distributed grids in Ukrainian war conditions. The situation in ukrainian power grid is characterized with overloaded and obsolete conventional power sources and transmission stations and chaotic development of renewable energy sources. The main task of this study is to help develop strategy of smart and efficient usage of newly build RES in preselected communities to help to stabilize the main network and to ensure higher energy resilience of particular municipalities. The paper deals with simulation and optimization of the energy community creation and with proposal of covering the energy needs. The case study is based on the set of preselected locations and shows the optimization process of proposed photovoltaic system for the power supply and high temperature battery for efficient energy storage.

articleTitle: Hydrogen Initiatives and Development
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article focuses on a giga-watt scale hydrogen factory. This factory will be in the USA, where the investor requested a study from ABB about the feasibility of this project. First, the article discusses the technology of electrolyzers which will be used. The second chapter focuses design of this giga-watt factory. The third chapter describes the block flow diagram and how each variance of the factory should look. And last section of this paper is about site selection and plot plan.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Ampacity of Overhead Power Lines Under the Conditions of the Electric Power System of the Slovak Republic
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The present investigation delved into the concept of ampacity, exploring its classification and practical implications. Methodological norms regulating ampacity were elucidated, alongside computations of both static and dynamic ampacity for prevalent conductors within the Slovak electric power system. Moreover, the study extended to determining the steady-state dynamic ampacity of a particular transmission line, considering its technical specifications within authentic meteorological settings on a chosen date.

articleTitle: Selected Problems of Modelling Energy Storage and Renewable Sources for Long-Term Analyses
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The development of power system models for long-term analyses require taking into account tool requirements, limitations of calculations and, at the same time, obtaining the best possible representations of parameters. This often requires appropriate preparations, including time-consuming adjustments on the part of researchers. The article presents the results related to the selection of the time series mapping method for modelling system development plans, in particular the assessment of the balance of renewable energy generation and energy storage.

articleTitle: A Simplified Urban-Scale Rooftop Photovoltaic Potential Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper aims to provide a simple yet effective estimate of urban-scale rooftop photovoltaic potential using only open-source software and publicly available data. The suggested methodology is presented in a sample location in Bratislava, Slovakia. Although many papers are published in similar areas, very few reveal the specific steps and functions in the software used, or the computational core of some part of the estimation is a paid service. Using our methodology, it is possible to obtain basic irradiation parameters and photovoltaic generation in the area. The great advantage of this model is its scalability and the easy way of modifying every computational parameter. The results and limitations of the proposed methodology are discussed, and further development is suggested.

articleTitle: Analysis of Dielectric Parameters of XLPE Insulation by Impedance Relaxation Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper discusses the analysis of dielectric parameters of XLPE insulation in cables using the impedance relaxation spectroscopy method. It discusses the measurement of individual frequency bands and the measurement methodology on different measuring devices. An analysis of the frequency dependence of the real permittivity and dielectric loss factor of new XLPE insulation samples has been carried out. The measurements were carried out at 10 V. The frequency range used was from 0.1 mHz to 10 kHz for the IDAX 300 and from 10 Hz to 2 MHz for the KEYSIGHT E4980A.

articleTitle: LabVIEW Virtual Instrument for the Command of an Adaptive Balancing Capacitive Compensator
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Two of the main concerns of distribution system operators and consumers regarding the power quality at the point of common coupling are power factor correction and load balancing. These problems can be addressed simultaneously by using unbalanced capacitive compensators which, in addition to the power factor correction, also balance the three-phase network load. The command of these compensators can be done using classic Programable Logical Controllers used on industrial scale in this field, which strictly implement the functions necessary for such a process. The paper presents a control solution for unbalanced capacitive compensators implemented by NI technology and LabVIEW graphical programming software. The solution is applied on a laboratory demonstration experimental model for an adaptive balancing capacitive compensator.

articleTitle: The Path to a Sustainable Power Production and Issues to Address
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: As climate change becomes increasingly obvious to the average person, meeting the European goals of carbon neutrality is more important than ever. However, for our power industry, this necessitates significant changes, mainly to accommodate the power production fluctuations of renewable energy sources. To shut down conventional coal-powered power plants, we will have to build new sources to cover our needs for electricity consumption and ensure their production does not disturb the grid's stability and reliability. All of these changes will bring many new challenges that we will have to face in the future to provide uninterrupted and quality power supply to every customer, as we do now. This paper aims to give an overview of the impact renewables have on the grid and provide possible solutions through modern technologies.

articleTitle: Verification of Night Road Safety Inspection by Luminance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article focuses on road safety in low visibility. Research is dedicated to the method of performing night road safety inspections and to comparison of its effectiveness and to the achieved outputs with measured data by the luminance analysis. The main objective of this study is to verify whether inadequate lighting of roadways can be identified solely through subjective visual perception. Both methods were compared in three test measurements in selected municipalities in the Czech Republic with different road lighting designs. Measured data from the luminance analyser were compared with technical standards defining the class of road lighting and subsequently compared with recorded traffic safety defects. The results confirm that it is possible to assess the lighting conditions of sites based on subjective perception of the night traffic area and can be considered valid. The final output also included a new graphical method of data interpretation in the form of implementation of the luminance analysis into cadastral maps.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Off-Grid System with Photovoltaic Panels
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article discusses the energy balance of an off-grid system and its optimization. To verify the proper operation of the system, it is necessary to measure its qualities and analyze measured data.

articleTitle: Sensorless in duction Motor Drive Based on Reactive Power MRAS Estimator Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes the problematics of modeling advanced methods of control of an induction machine such as sensorless control with the use of type of reactive power model reference adaptive system (Q-MRAS) observer with a neural network. In the beginning, problematics of the sensorless control of an induction machine is proposed, mainly in the way of MRAS possibilities with a specific description of Q-MRAS. Then, variants of Q-MRAS implementations are mentioned, also with the modern use of artificial neural networks within the structure of this type of observer. Further, there is described the realization of the simulation model of Q-MRAS observer containing the artificial neural network in Matlab Simulink interface. Simulations are made for the different values of the desired speed and its step changes. In conclusion, there is discussed the suitability of this type of observer due to the simulation results.

articleTitle: Impedance Measurement and Stability Analysis Based on Grid-Connected Inverter in D-Q Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the context of weak AC grids, the significant growth in installed capacity of renewable energy sources has intensified the interactions among inverters and their interaction with the AC grid, severely affecting the safe and stable operation of the grid system. In response to this issue, this paper takes a small-disturbance perspective and, based on the “black box” testing, conducts impedance measurements on the characteristics of inverters and the grid. Subsequently, employing the Nyquist stability criterion, the paper presents a thorough analysis of the potential ramifications associated with grid-connection in scenarios where the internal parameters of the inverter are unknown and the system operates within a weak grid environment. Finally, the result is validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Dielectric Analysis of a Polyurethane Enhanced by MgO or AlN Particles for an Application in Chemical Power Module Case
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This work briefly summarizes the influence of various weight percent of MgO nanoparticles and AlN microparticles in the polyurethane (PURs) sample on energy storage, energy dissipation, and relaxation time. The experiment results show almost comparable behaviour of PUR1+MgO and PUR2+AIN samples under certain conditions. The relative permittivity of PURs with particles is higher in comparison to the case of PURs without any additions. The temperature variations from 25° C to 120° C, implemented for AIN and MgO show an increase in energy dissipation with an increase in the temperature and vice versa. Meanwhile, with an increase in frequency in the range from 1 mHz to 1 MHz dielectric value becomes sufficiently less. To explain the behavior of dielectric spectra the Cole-Cole model and its various parameters were used. The a-relaxation and intermediate dipolar effect (IDE) of relaxation processes were observed during temperature measurements.

articleTitle: Modelling and Testing of Phasor Measurement Unit in PSCAD
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The advancement in phasor measurement technology brings new opportunities to improve the performance of applications that use wide area measurements. Most of these applications rely on simulation studies results. As a result, modelling and testing of PMUs are of high interest among electrical engineers and designers. In this paper, a PMU model based on discrete Fourier transform is presented and examined according to the measurement compliance in IEEE Std. C37.118.1 −2011. The model is implemented in PSCAD library. The results showed that the performance of this model has many advantages on the existing FFT block to monitor the phasor in PSCAD simulation environment. This model is expected to be used for simulation studies for testing and designing applications which use wide area synchrophasor measurements.

articleTitle: Wavelet Selection for Analysis of Acoustic Signals Emitted by Partial Discharges in Oil Insulation
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents and discusses wavelet selection for investigation on acoustic signals (AE) emitted by partial discharges (PD) in transformer mineral oil. The main aim of this research is to indicate the optimal wavelet regarding the accuracy of PD classification. Three scenarios are used to simulate different AE signal sources, including: point-plate PD source, air bubbles in oil and point-plate PD source with air bubbles in oil. All of the measurements were conducted under las conditions. AE signals emitted by each scenario were registered and processed using discreet wavelet transform (DWT) based on six different wavelet families. Finally, a support vector machine (SVM) classifier was used to classify the captured signals. As a result the highest accuracy was noted for the symlet wavelet. The presented results may be used to enhance the PD classification process using the AE method and potentially improve the diagnostics of PD in power transformers.

articleTitle: Speed Vectoring Algorithms for Drivelines with Multiple Modular E-Axles
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper discusses speed vectoring algorithms for drivelines containing multiple modular e-axles. The algorithm's purpose is to estimate the wheel and axle speeds of each e-axle in the driveline. The calculation is based on the vehicle's steering input, steering mode and driveline geometry. The algorithm is configurable for 4 × 4, 6 × 6 and 8 × 8 vehicle drivelines while also being compatible with conventional mechanical steering and electronically controlled systems. The steering modes built into the speed vectoring algorithm include front single-axle steering (FSAS), front twin-axle steering (FTAS), rear twin-axle steering (RTAS), crab steering (CBS), all-wheel-steering (AWS) and pivot steering (PTS). Each mode requires a separate steering geometry matrix. The paper highlights the main e-axle hardware considerations to be considered for speed vectoring before describing some of the steering modes implemented in the algorithm. The implications of varying wheel speeds on powertrain components are discussed and vehicle simulation for a variable radius turn is presented.

articleTitle: Grid Forming Inverter Models for Stability Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents inverter-based resource dynamic models. These models are suitable for grid forming inverters and applicable for dynamic stability studies of various types of resources - photovoltaics, battery systems, HVDC systems and STATCOMs. The simulations were conducted to verify the inverter models using various scenarios. These simulations were also performed for comparison in two simulation tools - MODES and PSS/E.

articleTitle: Power System Dynamic Model as a Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents dynamic model of electric power system (DMES) which is included in the dispatcher training simulator used by Czech transmission system operator. The purpose of the paper is also to prove if DMES fulfills the digital twin requirements.

articleTitle: Monitoring Level of Residual Currents in Dispatch System by New Function Embedded in Regulator of Arc-Suppression Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Increased capacitive earth fault currents due to the high level of overhead line cabling step-up demands for safe and reliable operation of compensated networks. The safety of compensated networks is closely related to residual current value. Last year, experimental measurements were carried out to verify the accuracy of a new method of residual current estimation by a regulator of an arc-suppression coil. The results of the experimental measurements proved that this method might be very accurate under some conditions. The main aim of this research paper is to present the results of an analysis that has been conducted to compare two methods from which the residual current can be determined. The emphasis is also put on the principle of operation of the newly designed function for a regulator of the arc-suppression coil.

articleTitle: Comparison of Hysteresis Current Control and VOC Control With SPWM and SVPWM Applied to Vienna Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes and compares 3 different control and modulation techniques for driving a 3-phase Vienna rectifier, with a focus on analysing its THD and FFT of resulted current and testing its behaviour during distorted grid. The modulations based on hysteresis current control, Voltage oriented control (VOC) based on sinusoidal PWM modulation (SPWM) and VOC based on Space Vector PWM modulation (SVPWM) were simulated and tested in PLECS simulation tool.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electric Vehicle Charging Process
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper aims to introduce readers to the issues surrounding electric vehicle (EV) charging and the potential problems arising from the expanding trend of electro mobility. It defines various EV charging methods, utilizing different types of charging stations and compatible connectors. Another key focus of this work is the set of options for controlling the power of charging stations at various levels, presenting power management strategies essential for the development of electro mobility worldwide. It is also dedicated to measuring EV charging and analyzing the collected data. Through measurements conducted in the professional laboratory of the Electrical Engineering Department at the Technical University of Kosice, the paper provides an objective view on the feedback effects of charging. It analyzes the charging of one electric vehicle, simulating the process of private home charging, and by examining the current charging of two electric vehicles, it simulates the process of mass public charging. The measurement results evaluate the feedback effects of both charging scenarios and offer recommendations for practice in future charging station construction. The exploration of the electric vehicle charging analysis has yielded numerous practical experiences, especially through expert consultations with employees of Vychodoslovenska distribucna a.s. Participating in laboratory measurements at the Smart Industry Lab and accessing measuring devices and evaluation software were immensely beneficial.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Reconfigurable Inverter Battery Systems for Aircraft Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The proliferation of electric vehicles for both passenger and cargo transportation in all aspects of life has resulted in the extensive utilization and investigation of various types of electrical power converters, with the aim of identifying the most optimal ones for specific applications based on parameters such as cost, complexity of control algorithms, power losses, reliability and many others. This paper evaluates the performance of three battery pack multilevel inverter topologies for aircraft applications using simulation results. The topologies under consideration are the Cross-Switched, Cascaded Half-Bridges, and Battery Modular Multilevel Management Converter. All three topologies enable the integration of the DC-AC converter, Battery Management System, and onboard charger functions on a single platform.

articleTitle: Influence of Water on Selected Dielectric Properties of Impregnants in the Cured State
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Improving the properties of impregnants used for the windings of electric rotating machines and transformers is still an actual problem that is being dealt with by many scientific institutions looking for more efficient and environmentally friendly materials. The goal is not only to increase the reliability and service life of electrical equipment, but also to optimize the production process and material base, which will lead to a reduction in economic costs. Constantly increasing requirements on the properties of impregnants are met either by introducing completely new impregnants or by modifying the original ones. In both cases, it is necessary to test their properties in order to verify the long-term stability and resistance to degradation effects. This paper presents partial results from testing the resistance of three different impregnants in the cured state to water in terms of investigation of selected dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Power Grid Security: N-1 Criterion and DACF Model
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper describes the individual network modelling mechanisms and measures for compliance with the N-1 security criterion for the exclusive transmission system operator in the Czech Republic, ČEPS. The main purpose of this paper is to describe the DACF process and the whole process for compliance with the safety criterion N-1 in terms of current and possible measures available to the dispatchers with the evaluation of specific situations from real operation.

articleTitle: Modelling of Road Lighting in Connection with VLC Requirements – Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article follows on from the article presented at the LS17 conference entitled “Case study – Modelling of Visible Light Communication (VLC) on Luminous Intensity Distribution Curve (LIDC) of LED Low Beam Car Headlamps”. This post dealt with the possibility of using VLC on roads with road lighting systems. In particular, it addressed the minimum light levels at which VLC can still be operated in the outdoor traffic area. These have been compared to the illuminance levels that can be achieved using LED low beam cars headlamps. It was mainly about the distance in front of the car at which it is able to distribute a useful VLC signal. The post addressed whether this technology is even possible to implement in relation to the distances that cars need to stop safely [1]. Since road lighting is also part of the night-time traffic space in cities and towns, this article will deal with its possibilities for implementing VLC in relation to the car communication with this infrastructure. This is made possible by the fundamental expansion of LED technologies, which have already penetrated not only light sources in automotive, but also road lighting [1]. The existing lighting systems of road lighting did not allow the application of VLC, because they were dominantly fitted with high-pressure sodium discharge lamps, which did not allow even slow regulation of the luminous flux, let alone fast switching (modulation) of the luminous flux at kHz levels and above. To demonstrate the possibilities of road lighting, a standard LED lighting system of road lighting with low levels of requirements according to European road lighting standards [EN 13201-2 Road lighting - Part 2: Performance requirements] and classification M5 was chosen for modelling.

articleTitle: Use of Satellite Imagery to Identify Light Pollution Sources in Urban Structure - the Limits and the Benefits
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper discusses the limits and benefits of satellite images used as a tool to identify sources of light pollution in the urban environments. It helps to detect the over illuminated or high-contrast zones that are often not obvious from human perspective, such as vertical landmarks illuminated by architectural lighting. Using the example of the historic centre of Karlovy Vary, a famous spa town in the Czech Republic, this study describes the process of data collection and evaluation, glare risk assessment and visual comfort of users. It identifies uncertainties and describes the benefits of the chosen approach.

articleTitle: Optimization of ESD Protection Design for Assembly Lines of Headlights Through Risk Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article addresses the requirements of ESD protection for sensitive components against electrostatic phenomena and describes a possible approach to defining ESD protective measures based on ESD risk analysis in a production line. When implementing ESD protection in a manufacturing facility according to current standards, there may be a need to tailor the standard control program to the specific situation based on the type of workplace. One way to customize is the design of ESD protective measures in the production line based on ESD risk analysis, which takes into account possible sources of risks and their consequences regarding the type of workplace. Such optimization of ESD protective measures design brings positive impacts in both technical and economic aspects.

articleTitle: Benford's Law in Electric Power Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Benford's Law (BL), predicting the distribution of leading digits in data, is applied in electric power engineering to detect irregularities in electricity consumption and fraud. It utilizes smart meter data for analyzing consumption patterns and predicting demand. Despite its advantages, challenges like small datasets and data manipulation exist. This abstract emphasizes BL's role in improving power system efficiency and security, highlighting the need for specialized approaches and interdisciplinary efforts to overcome its limitations in the electric power sector.

articleTitle: Water for Green Hydrogen Production
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Hydrogen is considered a powerful fuel for the future. Hydrogen production technologies vary widely. Green hydrogen is generated by electrolyzing water with electricity produced from renewable energy sources. According to the stoichiometry reaction, 9 kg of water is consumed to produce 1 kg of hydrogen. The water to be electrolysed has to meet stringent requirements and its preparation generates large quantities of wastewater, which should be managed appropriately. The objective of this research is to examine the methods by which water is prepared depending on its source and to determine the level of wastewater generated by its treatment. The results of the analyses carried out indicate that the water abstraction associated with green hydrogen production is significantly higher than the 9 kg per 1 kg of hydrogen value reported in numerous studies.

articleTitle: Optimizing Bidirectional AC Charging Efficiency of Multilevel Batteries: A Simulation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of bidirectional Alternating Current (AC) charging efficiency for modular Multilevel Inverter (MLI) based reconfigurable battery systems in the context of electromobility. This shall be achieved by the selection of a suitable Sub module (SM) topology within the MLI battery system. A simulation environment is developed to analyze the current Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), inverter efficiency, and battery efficiency of different MLI SM topologies. Specifically, comparisons are made between half bridge and Battery Modular Multilevel Management (BM3) SM topologies under various charging current and phase angle scenarios within the boundaries of the Type 2 Mode 3 charging standard of the European power grid. A boxed inverter design combined with a Cascaded H-Bridge (CHB) meso topology was used and peripheral influences through line resistance and line inductance were considered. Results indicate low THD values for both systems, with similar efficiencies close to theoretical maxima, albeit with slight advantages favoring the BM3 topology at higher currents. Battery efficiency remains consistently high, with marginal benefits favoring the BM3 system. Future research will explore the cost-effectiveness of employing multilevel systems for bidirectional AC charging, considering potential advantages over conventional AC onboard chargers.

articleTitle: Reliability Improvement with Automatic Transition Between Grid-Connected and Islanded Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: A power outage of the distribution network could cause large economic losses and safety hazards for industrial companies. Therefore, many industrial companies have a backup power source. Nevertheless, without automatic transition between grid-connected and islanded modes, there will be some time of outage of all consumers. In this article, calculations of the system average interruption duration index (SAIDI) were done and how it changes when automatic transition will be available. The low voltage and medium voltage SAIDI index values for the Czech largest distribution network operator were used as basic values for the calculations. It was calculated that the SAIDI index will improve from 307 min/year to 32 min/year with CHP as the hot reserve at a low voltage level and from 331 min/year to 35 min/year at a medium voltage level. It means a huge improvement in the reliability of the electric power supply. Automatic transition systems are especially worthwhile for companies and plants for whom interruption of production is very costly or a safety hazard.

articleTitle: Partial Anisotropy of Non-Oriented Electrical Steel Sheet as Cause of Shaft Voltage of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Shaft voltage is commonly found in induction motors. Shaft voltages occur in the motor, which is supplied by frequency inverter, but also in motors supplied directly from electrical network. The authors most often deal with occurrence of shaft voltages when supplying by frequency inverter. The literature also contains a lot of knowledge about the causes of shaft voltages, which occur during supplying directly from electrical network. In most cases, electrical or magnetic circuit unbalances due to motor design or shaft eccentricity are discussed as a cause of shaft voltages. Our article deals with the occurrence of shaft voltages due to the asymmetry of the magnetic circuit, which was caused by the partial anisotropy of the sheets, from which the stator and rotor packets are composed. The article also deals with the solution - by removing such magnetic asymmetry and thus induced shaft voltage.

articleTitle: Stochastic Modeling of a Residential PV Plant Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Increasing penetration of small renewable sources, especially in residential areas, brings significant challenges to the safe and reliable operation of distribution networks. PV plants are the prevailing type of sources installed on residential buildings. The power output of a PV plant is strongly dependent on actual meteorological conditions, that have naturally stochastic character. However, most methods currently used for feasibility studies and analysis of operating conditions in networks with renewable sources do not respect this stochastic nature, resulting in inaccurate or over-conservative results. This paper introduces a method for stochastic modeling of a residential PV plant's power output, allowing a more objective evaluation of network conditions in low-voltage distribution networks. The paper also discusses the main factors influencing the accuracy of the method and defines basic requirements for the quality of input data.

articleTitle: Train Approach Detection System Based on Track Impedance Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper presents the principle used in the development of a device for measuring the distance of a train from a level crossing, which is based on the measured impedance of the track circuit shorted by a train axle i.e. based on the measurements of the real parameters of a track circuit. A hardware simulation model of the track circuit was built and used during the development of the measurement device. This paper concludes by presenting the results of a pilot operation of the measuring device on a real track and shows the measured impedance and phase waveforms obtained when a train passes a level crossing.

articleTitle: Diagnostic Methods of Photovoltaic Panels: Low-cost Electroluminescence
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Currently, there is a rapid increase in the installed capacity of photovoltaic (PV) power plants around the world. However, with the increasing number of PV plants, it is necessary to keep in mind their safe and reliable operation. As photovoltaic panels gradually age, they degrade and develop various defects that can result in reduced performance or even shut down the plant. This causes financial losses. To detect these faults early, there are several diagnostic methods that allow early detection, thereby increasing the efficiency of the operation. The most commonly used methods of PV panel diagnostics are described in this paper. A major part of the text is devoted to electroluminescence. The main part deals with the easy modification of a commercial camera for the purpose to perform diagnostics in low-cost conditions.

articleTitle: Operation of Public Lighting Networks at Voltage Lower than Nominal
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Public lighting networks (PLNs) play a crucial role in urban infrastructure, directly impacting safety and comfort. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of PLN operation at reduced voltage, considering factors such as voltage drop, line parameters, and component capabilities. A case study demonstrates the feasibility of operating PLNs with a wide voltage range, offering insights into potential benefits and challenges. Overall, the study underscores the potential of innovative operational models to enhance the efficiency and reliability of public lighting networks.

articleTitle: The Importance of Heat Pumps and Cogeneration for the Transformation of the Energy Sector to Sustainable Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with possible solutions to heating demand coverage. It compares the usual solution of heating by combustion boilers with the possible use of more advanced technologies. These technologies are cogeneration units and heat pumps: through their appropriate use and control, it is possible to achieve significant savings in primary fuels. Heat is needed especially in winter; it is therefore optimal to operate cogeneration during this period. Produced electricity can then be used to compensate seasonal drops in solar photovoltaic production. Increasing energy efficiency and the use of renewable sources can significantly contribute to the transformation of the energy sector toward sustainable sources.

articleTitle: Comparing of Potential Energy from the Sun During a Year in Czechia and Vietnam
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Electrical lighting has transformed human society, enabling activities to take place before sunset and improving safety and productivity in many contexts. However, the generation and use of electricity can also have significant environmental impacts, including greenhouse gas emissions and pollution. To mitigate these impacts, many countries are increasingly turning to renewable energy sources, such as Photovoltaic (PV) power. PV power is an attractive source of energy because it is renewable, abundant, and widely distributed. However, the amount of PV energy available varies depending on a range of factors, including latitude, weather patterns, and time of year. In order to better understand the potential for PV power in different regions, it is important to compare the amount of power that can be generated from the sun at different locations. In this paper, we compare the power from the sun during a year in two countries: Czechia and Vietnam. These two countries were chosen because they have different latitudes, climates, and levels of Solar irradiation. Czechia is a landlocked country in central Europe, with a temperate climate and significant seasonal variations in sunlight. Vietnam, on the other hand, is a tropical country in Southeast Asia, with a year-round humid climate and high levels of sunlight. By comparing the power from the sun in these two countries, we aim to provide insights into the potential for PV power in different regions, and to identify factors that influence the amount of power that can be generated from the sun. Overall, this study aims to contribute to our understanding of the PV energy potential of different regions and the need for tailored approaches to PV power generation that take into account the specific environmental, economic, and social contexts.

articleTitle: Areas of Impact of Nodal Powers on Power Flows in a Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The problem, which is solved in the paper, is clustering in a power system. Existing solutions to this problem have a number of shortcomings. The paper presents considerations leading to the development of a more advantageous method than the existing clustering methods. In those considerations, the authors take into account the impact of nodal powers on branch powers in the power system. The use of the developed method is shown on the example of clustering for the IEEE 14 Bus Test Case. A discussion of the properties of the method ends the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Selected Parameters of Midel 7131 Ester with Addition of Aluminum Oxide Al2O3
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents studies on the effect of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> aluminum oxide on the water content, breakdown voltage, dielectric loss factor tgδ at 90 ̊ C and acid number of the electroinsulating liquid, which in this case is the synthetic ester Midel 7131. It was also investigated what effect the addition of surfactants (oleic acid, ROKwinol 80 and TritonX) to the prepared nanofluids had. All samples were tested in the same way, according to the standards presented in the paper. The motivation to undertake the described research is the noticeable increase in articles on nanofluids and the wide field for the creation of various colloidal liquids, while there are still gaps in the literature describing the mechanisms of influence of nanoparticles on the physicochemical parameters of the base liquids used.

articleTitle: ANN Stabilization of Negative-Sequence Integral Protection of Power Transformers for Turn-to-Turn Winding Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The negative-sequence differential current integral principle supplemented with appropriate asymmetry indices is a very sensitive technique for detecting turn-to-turn faults (TTFs) in transformer windings. In this paper, an ANN-based stabilization function for such a protection scheme is introduced. The developed technique offers effective stabilization during transformer energization and recovery inrush after fault clearing, preserving the required sensitivity for TTFs.

articleTitle: Medium Voltage Covered Conductors: Advantages, Disadvantages and High Impedance Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Covered conductors represent an alternative to classic ACSR for overhead high-voltage distribution lines. They were first put into operation in the 1970s, especially in the USA and Europe at voltage levels up to 35 kV. Since the 1990s, with the spread of covered conductors with multi-layer insulation, they have gradually been deployed at even higher voltage levels. The constant growth of electricity consumption in combination with the planned development of electromobility and decentralized sources will place ever higher demands on the reliability of the medium voltage distribution network. Therefore, in order to increase the reliability and safety of operation, in 2014 work was started at VŠB-TUO on the development of an high impedance fault detector for these lines. Its development has continued since then, this work represents some of the experience from the development and long-term operation of this device.

articleTitle: Computational Model of Hydrogen PEM Fuel Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the description of the created computational model of hydrogen PEM fuel cells (in the MathLab App Designer software), which are part of the commercially available production module (hydrogen micro-cogeneration unit) FCS 8-XXL manufactured by Nedstack. These specific production units are operated as part of a hybrid energy system in the Laboratory of Hydrogen Technologies of VŠB-TUO, where they are used for the energy use of hydrogen gas, which is produced by electrolysis of water fed from available renewable sources (primarily a photovoltaic power plant). The control of the mentioned fuel cells is ensured by a sophisticated control system, which also uses the computational model described here, which enables reliable and safe operation of the low-temperature fuel cell modules integrated into the energy system.

articleTitle: Two-Winding Transformer in Symmetrical Components
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with the issue of symmetrical components in transformers, considering various winding connections in the occurrence of different types of faults. The transformer is a determining element for the connection of the equivalent model in the zero-sequence and, therefore, also determines the magnitude of the impedance in the zero-sequence and the magnitude of the zero-sequence current. The equivalent model in the zero sequence primarily affects fault currents and voltage in the electrical grid during the most common fault, the phase-to-ground fault. The theory of component systems is well-known and widely published. This paper aims to explain the properties of a two-winding transformer in symmetrical component systems based on the results of simulations implemented in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Transition of Inverter Generating Plants to Unintentional Island Operation in Part of the Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the issue of unintentional islanding in distribution networks with inverter-interfaced decentralized sources. Typically, these are photovoltaic power plants in low or medium voltage networks. A part of the research framework is presented in which the authors are concerned with verifying the ability of inverters to prevent unintentional islanding. A number of inverters from several manufacturers applying various techniques to detect islanded operation have been verified. The tests were carried out at the test facility at Brno University of Technology and the test methodology is based on well-known standards designed for this verification. The obtained results are presented and evaluated; the conclusion provides their summarization as well as recommendations for further research directions.

articleTitle: Comparative Study between Model-in-the-Loop Offline and Real-Time Simulations for Phasor Measurement Units
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Today's distribution networks are transitioning from traditional power grids with passive loads and unidirectional power flow to more complex active distribution networks (ADNs) with high penetration of intermittent distributed energy resources (DERs) and loads with fast-changing dynamics. These changes made the distribution system's planning, control, and monitoring very challenging defying existing control tools such as Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA). The deployment of Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) in electrical networks constitutes a powerful tool in mitigating the faced challenges. This paper analyses and tests the PMU block provided in the library of the R2021b Matlab together with a proposed PMU model, in different system working conditions, using model-in-the-loop (MIL) offline and real-time simulations.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Operation of Portable Traffic Monitoring Devices Using Photovoltaic Panels for Sustainability and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The aim of the study was to investigate the possibilities of extending the operation of portable devices designed to monitor road traffic during short-term measurements, while keeping handling and installation simple. Of interest were the specific possibilities of using photovoltaic (PV) panels to extend the operation of measuring devices. The use of solar energy is assumed to achieve a significant extension of device operation by up to 50 %. The methodology of the study involves the interconnection of photovoltaic panels in conjunction with portable devices to achieve sufficient power to extend the operating time. In real operation, the efficiency of photovoltaic panels was evaluated by focusing on analytical procedures. The results of the study can provide advances in road traffic monitoring and offer practical solutions for the efficient and sustainable operation of portable devices.

articleTitle: Control of Outdoor Lighting Systems with Long-Distance Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article describes the problem of control of outdoor lighting systems in electrical stations of a transmission system. It describes the problems of controlling lighting systems using the DALI standard. Due to the large size of the power station, long distance communication must be ensured. This article deals with the individual possibilities of communication with luminaires. The operation of the lighting system of the electrical stations of the transmission system is monitored by a programmable logic controller (PLC) control system, which allows for the control and diagnostics of individual types of lighting. The main reasons for controlling lighting systems are energy savings, proper visibility of the camera system, and reduction of light pollution.

articleTitle: Cost-Effectiveness of Heat Pump in Apartment Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: We live in a time when energy prices in general have stabilized, but they are incomparably higher than a few years ago. In terms of household energy costs, the largest items are the energy needed for heating and hot water. If a person lives in a family home, he or she has a relatively free choice as to which primary energy source to use for these purposes. However, the situation is different if we live in apartment buildings, which historically are in most cases connected to the system of the district heat supply (DHS). In this case, our options are limited in many respects. This article describes what led the residents of one particular apartment building 7 years ago to decide to disconnect from the district heat supply and choose a different heat source. At the same time, this article provides a more comprehensive view of this issue in terms of legislation, technical feasibility and the payback period (PBP) of the investment in the Czech Republic.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Flows in a Building With Non-Linear Loads and a Hybrid Photovoltaic Power Plant With Battery Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the evaluation of the power quality in a multipurpose building CPIT-TL3 equipped with many non-linear appliances and a hybrid photovoltaic power plant (HPVPP). During the control reading of the power consumption from the electricity meters, discrepancies in the current and power values measured by the main electricity meter of the building and the HPVPP metering system were found. For this reason, measurements were made using power quality analysers. The measurements revealed a significantly distorted current draw with a low power factor. Selected measurement results and their analysis are presented in this paper. Although the significantly distorted current did not affect the quality of the supply voltage, the reduction of current distortion will need to be addressed. The multipurpose building is primarily used for scientific and research purposes; therefore, the distortion of the drawn current should be as low as possible.

articleTitle: Positive Impact of the OLTC Blocking on the Voltage Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The contribution deals with the issue of the impact of the blocking of the automatic voltage regulator (AVR) on the TS/DS transformers located between the transmission and distribution system on the voltage stability of the transmission system (TS) in the event of a voltage decrease in the nodes of the TS. The contribution is a partial collaboration with the Slovak transmission system operator (TSO) Slovenská elektrizačná prenosová sústava, a.s. regarding to the assessment of voltage stability considering the scenario of increasing transit through TS SR.

articleTitle: Testing, Analysis and Diagnostics of Chosen Faults of Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper is focused on the analysis and detection of faults of photovoltaic (PV) elements, especially PV modules, and their impact on the reliable operation of the photovoltaic system. Brief overview of currently used measurement techniques and methods in photovoltaic diagnostics is introduced. The consequences for the safe and reliable supply of electricity from the PV system were demonstrated on silicon photovoltaic modules by modelled faults and evaluate them using selected diagnostic methods. The influence of respective defects and environmental impact was demonstrated using current-voltage (I-V) curves, impedance spectroscopy and thermography. The aim was not to quantify the deterioration of measured samples, but to demonstrate chosen methods and their potential.

articleTitle: Road Lighting Regulation in Relation to Vertical Illuminance and Vehicle Stopping Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with a model situation of a traffic area illuminated by a combination of vehicle low beam headlamps and luminaires of road lighting. In the model situation, the distribution of vertical illuminance in front of the vehicle located directly below the luminaire was evaluated. When the vehicle is positioned below the luminaire, the shortest distances in front of the vehicle occur, in which conditions are sufficient for obstacle detection. The model boundary conditions chosen represented the least favorable situation in terms of visibility in the traffic area. The aim of the study was to evaluate the visibility in the area in front of the vehicle during the operation of the luminaires of road lighting with the regulation of luminous flux output. The main motivation for the operation of luminaires of road lighting is to save electrical energy and are justified by the decrease in traffic volume during late night hours. However, is it appropriate to implement dimming of luminaires without taking into account the visibility of obstacles in the traffic area [1], [2] depending on the stopping distance affected by the maximum permissible vehicle speed?

articleTitle: Mathematical Models of Multiphase Machines Based on Symmetrical Components Decomposition in Relation to Space Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper covers the theory of symmetrical components decomposition in relation to spatial wave harmonics produced in the airgap of multiphase machines. Easy to follow algorithm for obtaining transformation matrixes of multiphase machines is proposed. As an example, mathematical models of five-phase and asymmetrical six-phase induction machines are presented.

articleTitle: Long-Term Analysis of Development and Demand for Energy Storage in Poland
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article presents approach used to model energy storages in long term analyses. These analyses focus on assessment of required storages capacities to ensure stable performance of power system and to avoid unserved energy on one hand and wasting surplus of electricity generated in renewable sources on the other hand.

articleTitle: Static Line Rating of Overhead Power Lines in Various European Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article compares the static line rating (SLR) values defined for overhead power lines in various European countries. The results reveal significant variations in SLR values between different countries, highlighting the impact of varying limit conditions on the determination of SLR. Wind speed and direction were identified as critical factors that influence the SLR value, with minor changes in these parameters resulting in significant differences in conductor temperature. Moreover, the influence of wind speed on conductor temperatures highlights the need for expert discussion and analysis when considering changes to SLR limit conditions. Adjusting the wind speed to values above 0.6 m/s or altering the wind direction on the conductor can potentially increase overhead power line capacity.

articleTitle: Real-Time Electrical Energy Balancing and Limiting the Peak Power Demand of an Industrial Facility Using a Multi-Agent System - Early Solutions of the DIEGO Project
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper raises the problem of real-time electrical energy balancing and limiting the peak power demand at the level of the considered factory. Solution of the problem is important from technical and economic point of view, especially when existing renewable energy source and electrical energy storage system are taken into account. Studies concerning this question are conducted within the DIEGO project (details in acknowledgments). First, the paper analyses the internal electric power grid in the considered factory and presents a general characteristics of technological processes realized there. Next, the paper presents analysis of daily load and generation curves in the scope of active and reactive energy and characterizes practicable preventive measures (methods) for reducing peak electric loads at the level of the considered factory. Multi-Agent Systems are considered to be implemented for the purpose. Presented work is part of greater understanding which results will be further published.

articleTitle: Analyzing Software Tools to Assess Optimal Variant of Energy Store
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Energy storage systems (ESSs) are a key component of a power system that can serve as a means to reduce energy consumption and improve the efficiency and sustainability of renewable energy sources. The purpose of this paper is to evaluate open source software tools, in particular Python-based ones, to evaluate the most suitable energy storage solutions regarding economic and technical parameters. PyPSA (Python for Power System Analysis) is a free software tool that has proven to be a versatile and powerful tool for modeling, simulating, and optimizing modern power systems, integrating renewables, and evaluating energy storage systems. Its open source nature, along with its comprehensive documentation and support, has facilitated its application in a variety of real-world applications and case studies around the world.

articleTitle: A Review of Photovoltaic Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Various advances have been made in the photovoltaic industry. Even though there are technological improvements, there are many problems that this industry faces. The main aim of this article is to study the PV working principles and their existing technologies. This article discusses the Photovoltaic Effect, the process of manufacturing Solar cells, state-of-the-art PV technologies, common faults of the existing technologies, and how to gain the maximum efficiency output from the solar cells. Upon discussing these topics, finally, an in-depth analysis will be made of these problems and provide solutions to overcome these problems.

articleTitle: Harmonic Filter Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on the pivotal role of Harmonic Filters (HFs) in mitigating harmonic distortion within electrical systems to enhance power quality and efficiency. Harmonic distortion, characterized by deviations from the ideal sinusoidal waveform of electrical power, can cause equipment malfunctions, overheating, and a reduced lifespan of infrastructure. HFs, known for their cost-effectiveness and simplicity, employ inductors, capacitors, and resistors to selectively reduce specific harmonic frequencies, thereby improving system reliability and performance. The document explores traditional design methodologies of harmonic filter design, emphasizing criteria and considerations critical for effective harmonic mitigation. It highlights the use of advanced simulation tools, such as MATLAB/Simulink and PF DigSilent, which enable precise analysis and optimization of filter designs to meet specific system requirements. Moreover, it discusses the significance of designing filters with adequate margins to ensure system safety and reliability, considering the variability of loads and the presence of other harmonic sources. Driven by the necessity to enhance harmonic filter design in the face of increasingly complex electrical infrastructures, this paper advocates for leveraging recent advances in simulation tools.

articleTitle: Heat Pump Performance Design for Heating System in the Building
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with heating system powered by a heat pump. It presents a basic theoretical knowledge and principle of operation. The heat losses of the building and the specific heat flux are calculated on a practical example of a family house. Based on these values, it is further shown how the heat pump performance is designed to provide underfloor heating.

articleTitle: Complementary Reactive Power Control of Three-Phase AC/DC Voltage Source Converters for Grid Support Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This research investigates the role of voltage source converters (VSCs) in providing reactive power support in power systems. With the increasing integration of power electronics-based loads (PELs) and distributed generation (DG), the traditional emphasis on reactive power management becomes critical to maintaining system stability and efficiency. While effective and traditional solutions such as STATCOMs are often centralized and costly, this study focuses on the use of voltage source rectifiers (VSRs) deployed at various interfaces to provide reactive power support. A three-phase 100 kW VSR model is implemented using vector control techniques to provide adjustable reactive power output in range of +/-45 kvar under various supply voltage and loading scenarios. The results show that the VSR controlled by vector control techniques effectively regulates the AC side reactive power while maintaining a stable DC side voltage. The study demonstrates the feasibility of using VSRs for distributed reactive power support in power systems.

articleTitle: In-Field Compliance Testing of an Existing Photovoltaic Power Generating Module
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on discussion of in-field compliance testing power generating modules (PGMs) within Czechia. Firstly, it describes compliance testing methods that can be used either in laboratory setting or in-field on a PGM connected to a real network. Then, requirements are discussed in the scope of their suitability for the in-field testing. In what follows, architecture of a photovoltaic PGM is discussed and requirements assigned to responsible component are categorized. As some requirements are associated with the approach and practice of specific distribution systems, distribution system operators in Czechia and the difference among their requirements in the scope of in-field testing is summarized. Lastly, the test setup and the authors’ experience with in-field testing are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Stand-alone Hybrid Power Plant for Ancillary Services Provision
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Changes in the generation mix will increase fluctuation of power balance in energy systems and simultaneously will decrease available resources of Ancillary services (AnS) to stabilize those fluctuations. Renewable resources (RES) are not primarily designed to provide AnS. Thus, alternative AnS resources has to be found or built to prevent a shortfall in available AnS capacities. An ideal AnS provider is independent on internal or external circumstances and provides services with high availability and reliability. Such requirements may fulfill a stand-alone hybrid powerplant designed as virtual power plant (VPP) only for AnS provision, comprised of battery energy storage system (BESS) and small spinning generators. The generators are stopped and ready to start when there is no significant demand for AnS, which challenges operation of the power plant: the service demand is unknown in term of activation time and required power, optimal scheduling of generator operation (up-time) is crucial both for cost efficiency and service provision quality. Robust control algorithm is introduced in this paper using rolling time window, demand interpreter, scheduling module and real time power adjustment module.

articleTitle: Active Planning of Flexible and Cohesive Virtual Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 24th International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on using multi-objective, bi-level, mixed-integer optimization process for active planning in active distribution networks based on virtual microgrids. The authors optimize the planning of an Active Distribution Network by configuring distributed generation and energy storage systems to cope with the stochastic uncertainty caused by forecast errors in wind speed and loads. To do this, flexibility reserves are needed, and the authors quantify the relationship between flexibility and uncertainty by defining an innovative cohesion index. This index is used to penalize operational costs and improve system self-sufficiency. Based on the optimization result of a real-world 240-bus distribution network in Midwest U.S., case studies are made to show the importance of including the Virtual Microgrid cohesion and flexibility.
